neighbours.label: a past-tense communication act by a source: 'wrote', 'said', 'asked', 'talked to', 'told' after a named person or reporter; the same subjects with a non-communication verb stay quiet
fire: In 1958, the historian Ruth Ellis wrote that the war had changed nothing.
To understand the delay, we spoke to Ben Ortiz, a port manager.
The farmers gathered in the square and asked the governor for seed.
Speaking on radio, the coach Mark Dunn said the team was tired.
As the poet Mary Oliver once wrote, attention is a form of devotion.
Our reporter talked to three nurses about the night shift.
The judge told the jury to ignore the last remark.
Years later, the explorer Hans Berg wrote a letter to the king.
quiet: In 1958, the historian Ruth Ellis moved to a farm near the coast.
To understand the delay, we drove to the port and parked near the gate.
The farmers gathered in the square and waited for the rain.
Earlier this season, the coach Mark Dunn bought a new house.
As a young girl, the poet Mary Oliver walked the woods every day.
Our reporter drove past three hospitals on the way home.
The judge locked the door of the courtroom at noon.
Years later, the explorer Hans Berg built a cabin by the lake.
